summary: The Planet's Early Warning System is a WebGIS platform that prevents false wildfire alarms as NASA’s legacy MODIS (1 km) satellite retires and transitions to sharper VIIRS (375 m) sensors. Using LightGBM Quantile Regression trained on 18.87M detections (R^2 = 0.8833) across 0.5^\circ grid cells, it translates MODIS readings into VIIRS equivalents with 80% confidence intervals, while Isolation Forest flags dangerous nocturnal fire surges. This is important because protects climate baselines and equips responders and researchers with live 24h feeds, split-view satellite comparisons
details:
The Planet's Early Warning System is an AI-powered wildfire harmonization and early-warning WebGIS platform. It bridges historical and modern NASA satellite fire records, detects abnormal night-time fire surges in real time, estimates burned biomass and \text{CO}_2 emissions, and generates operational reports and standardized datasets for emergency responders and climate researchers.

How It Works

* Data Ingestion: Fetches live 24-hour NASA FIRMS global fire detections or processes custom raw satellite CSV uploads.

* Spatial Unification: Aggregates scattered fire detections into standardized 0.5^\circ \times 0.5^\circ geographic grid cells for consistent historical baseline comparisons.

* Cross-Sensor AI Harmonization: Uses a LightGBM Quantile Regression model—trained on 18.87 million detections across 293,719 grid cells in five global fire regions (USA, Canada, Brazil, Greece, and Australia) at R^2 = 0.8833—to translate legacy MODIS (1 km) readings into VIIRS-equivalent (375 m) intensities alongside an 80% confidence interval ([Q10, Q90]).

* Nocturnal Anomaly Detection: Evaluates incoming telemetry with an unsupervised Isolation Forest model (0–1 anomaly severity score) to flag fires that persist or intensify after sunset.

* Interactive Visualization & Reporting: Displays results on a 3D orbital globe, a seasonal burning calendar, and an interactive map

* Eliminates False Surges: Solves the MODIS-to-VIIRS calibration gap

* Quantifies Uncertainty: Provides [Q10, Q90] confidence bounds for every grid cell

* Actionable Field & Research Outputs: Delivers immediate nocturnal containment-loss alerts

* Accessible & Reliable: Supports colorblind-safe thermal palettes

* Preserve multi-decadal wildfire climate continuity across retiring and modern NASA Earth observation sensors.
